Cultural impact
Part of the New Hollywood film-making wave, Kubrick's films are considered by film historian Michel Ciment to be
"among the most important contributions to world cinema in the twentieth century", and he is frequently cited as one of
the greatest and most influential film directors. According to film historian Robert Kolker, Leading directors, including

<color=#3366CC>Martin Scorsese</color>, <color=#3366CC>Steven Spielberg</color>, <color=#3366CC>Wes Anderson</color>, <color=#3366CC>George Lucas</color>, <color=#3366CC>James Cameron</color>, <color=#3366CC>Terry Gilliam</color>, the <color=#3366CC>Coen brothers</color>,
<color=#3366CC>Ridley Scott</color>, and <color=#3366CC>George A. Romero</color>, have cited Kubrick as a source of inspiration, and additionally in the case of
Spielberg and Scott, collaboration. Steven Spielberg comments that the way Kubrick "tells a story is antithetical to the
way we are accustomed to receiving stories" and that "nobody could shoot a picture better in history". Orson Welles,
one of Kubrick's greatest personal influences and favorite directors, said that: "Among those whom I would call
'younger generation', Kubrick appears to me to be a giant."
Kubrick continues to be cited as a major influence by many directors, including Brad Bird, <color=#3366CC>Christopher Nolan</color>, Todd

Field, <color=#3366CC>David Fincher</color>, <color=#3366CC>Guillermo del Toro</color>, <color=#3366CC>David Lynch</color>, <color=#3366CC>Lars von Trier</color>, <color=#3366CC>Tim Burton</color>, <color=#3366CC>Michael Mann</color>, <color=#3366CC>Gaspar Noé</color>, and
Don Hertzfeldt.
Artists in fields other than film have also expressed admiration for Kubrick. English musician and poet <color=#3366CC>PJ Harvey</color>
argued that "something about [...] what is not said in his films...there's so much space, so many things that are silent –
and somehow, in that space and silence everything becomes clear. With every film, he seems to capture the essence
of life itself". The music video for <color=#3366CC>Kanye West</color>'s 2010 song "Runaway" was inspired by Eyes Wide Shut. Pop singer
<color=#3366CC>Lady Gaga</color>'s concert shows have included dialogue, costumes, and music from A Clockwork Orange.
Tributes
In 2000, BAFTA renamed their Britannia lifetime achievement award the "Stanley Kubrick Britannia Award". Many
people who worked with Kubrick created the 2001 documentary Stanley Kubrick: A Life in Pictures, produced and
directed by Kubrick's brother-in-law, Jan Harlan.
The first public exhibition of material from Kubrick's personal archives was presented jointly in 2004 by the Deutsches
Filmmuseum and Deutsches Architekturmuseum in Frankfurt, Germany, in cooperation with Christiane Kubrick and Jan
Harlan / The Stanley Kubrick Estate. In 2009, an exhibition of paintings and photos inspired by Kubrick's films was held
in <color=#3366CC>Dublin</color>, Ireland. On October 30, 2012, an exhibition devoted to Kubrick opened at the Los Angeles County Museum
of Art and concluded in June 2013. In October 2013, the Brazil São Paulo International Film Festival staged an exhibit
of his work and a retrospective of his films. The exhibit opened at the <color=#3366CC>Toronto International Film Festival</color> (TIFF) in late
2014 and ended in January 2015.
Kubrick is widely referenced in popular culture; for example, the TV series <color=#3366CC>The Simpsons</color> is said to contain more
references to Kubrick films than any other pop culture phenomenon. When the Directors Guild of Great Britain gave
Kubrick a lifetime achievement award, they included a sequence of all the homages from the show. Several works have
been created that related to Kubrick's life, including the made-for-TV mockumentary Dark Side of the Moon (2002),
which is a parody of the conspiracy theory that Kubrick had been involved with the faked footage of the NASA Moon
landings. Colour Me Kubrick (2005) was authorized by Kubrick's family and starred John Malkovich as Alan Conway, a
con artist who had assumed Kubrick's identity in the 1990s. In the 2004 film The Life and Death of Peter Sellers,
Kubrick was portrayed by Stanley Tucci.
In April 2018, the <color=#3366CC>International Astronomical Union</color> named the largest mountain of <color=#3366CC>Pluto</color>'s moon <color=#3366CC>Charon</color> after Kubrick.
